subject: Workplace Skills
title: Rituals Replace Watercoolers
description: A 60-second lesson on Rituals Replace Watercoolers.

hook.text: A remote team starts every Monday with a two-minute 'weekend highlight.' Engagement is higher than their in-office.

buildup.text: Office culture happens through shared experiences: lunch, commute stories, birthday cakes. Remote culture needs design.

discovery.text: Small weekly rituals create belonging: show-and-tell, pet-cam Fridays, or themed Slack channels for hobbies.

twist.text: Forced fun backfires. The best rituals emerge from what teams naturally enjoy, not mandates from leadership.

climax.text: Ask your team: what small ritual would make Mondays better? Let them own it. Participation follows ownership.

punchline.text: Design the culture. Remote teams don't grow one by accident.

quiz.question: Why do remote teams need intentional rituals?
options: Culture happens naturally in offices but must be designed remotely
Remote workers have more free time for social activities
